data: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"result":{"capabilities":{"logging":{},"resources":{"listChanged":true},"tools":{"listChanged":true}},"instructions":"You are connected to Tessryx, where the user builds and publishes web apps in their own workspace. It looks like a CMS — people edit content through editors generated from the schemas you write — and the same resources make up the live app: its pages, the API routes those pages use, and the data behind them, served at public URLs. What you author here, the user gets as both a running site and an editable CMS.

The resources, each authored, versioned and published like code:
- schemas — JSON Schemas that validate datafiles and generate the human editor.
- datafiles — schema-validated JSON: the app's content and data, which people can edit.
- workflows — the logic behind a page or an API route: it renders HTML or returns JSON from the app's data.
- dynamic endpoints — publish a workflow at a public URL with its input and cache settings; one serves a page, another an API route the page's own script uses.
- api templates — a saved, versioned connection to one of the user's own services, for their workflows to use.
- secrets — credentials the user stores in the app for those connections; you see their names, never their values.
- schedules — keep the app's data fresh on a timer, through a workflow.
- apps — group a project's resources into one editing surface.

A page can be rendered on the server from its data, or load its data in the browser and call its own API routes.

Every definition has a published format; read it before writing one — get_workflow_definition_schema, get_dynamic_endpoint_definition_schema, get_api_template_definition_schema, get_schedule_definition_schema, get_app_definition_schema. The same format generates the human's editor. Save a new resource with its create tool and changes as new versions, then publish (publish=true does both). Check a workflow with validate_workflow and try a draft version before publishing it. To take something down, use its unpublish or delete tool.

Your endpoints serve at https://<your-tenant>.tessryx.app/<endpoint-slug> ; assets embed by their absolute $asset.url (https://<your-tenant>.tessryxusermedia.com/<path>), where <your-tenant> is the tenant_slug whoami returns. All tools are scoped to your own workspace — you never pass tenant identity. CALL whoami first to confirm the current user and workspace; if no workspace is attached, every data tool will refuse until the user sets one up.

Some steps only a human can do — give the user the link, don't just describe it: create/join a workspace https://tessryx.io/dashboard ; create a secret or set its value https://tessryx.io/dashboard/secrets ; upload a binary you were not given https://tessryx.io/dashboard/media.

The guides explain each resource in depth (read them before building): get_guide, with list_guides for the topics — overview (read first), build-a-page, build-a-blog, authoring (lifecycle, patch_workflow, clean definitions, delete≠cascade), then one per resource — workflows (expressions/assets/output), datafiles (bind-vs-fetch, @latest trap, list-at-scale), api-templates (HTTP/gRPC, secrets), endpoints (input modes, POST, caching, gated/members-only pages), apps (grouping), plus schemas, schedules, custom-domains.","protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","serverInfo":{"name":"tessryx-mcp-gateway","title":"Tessryx","version":"1.0.0","websiteUrl":"https://tessryx.io","icons":[{"src":"https://mcp.tessryx.io/icon.svg","mimeType":"image/svg+xml","sizes":["any"]}]}}}
